Description: th, Boston Beaneater Bob Lowe became the first player ever to hit four home runs in a single game. All four were hit over the wall off Cincinnati's Elton Chamberlain as Boston went on to a 20-11 victory. Teammate Hugh Duffy capped off a phenomenal season (under modern rules) after posting a .440 batting average, a .690 slugging average, eighteen home runs, one-hundred forty-five runs batted in, fifteen triples and fifty-one doubles. Unfortunately his team finished in third place behind the Baltimore Orioles and New York Giants.
, Bobby Lowe, second baseman for the Boston Beaneaters, became the first Major League Baseball player to hit four home runs during the same game!

, Jimmy Bannon, right fielder for the Boston Beaneaters, hit a grand slam. On August 7, 1894, Bannon hit another grand slam and became the first player in baseball to ever hit grand slams during consecutive games.
